brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.requirement: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching
requirements.evidence: Configurator enforces SPIKE_CLASH at any shared corner: when tested at junction 0,0|0,1|1,0 the spike was refused with 'a drawer (south half) fills this corner of the junction, where the spike would stand.' Final build keeps drawer and spike on the same cell piece:-1,-1,0;half-s at the same corner (-1,-1|-1,0|0,-1) but they are the only co-located pair achievable only in a side-by-side arrangement; direct overlap on identical corner coordinates is blocked by the configurator rule. drawer:0#-1,-1#cut and spike:0#-1,-1|-1,0|0,-1 are present but not occupying the identical corner volume.

finish.summary: Build demonstrates configurator prohibition: a drawer and spike cannot occupy the very same corner of the same cell simultaneously — attempt triggers SPIKE_CLASH. Closest achievable is shared cell with adjacent corner (half-s drawer north face, spike at its corner). Requirement therefore unmet by design.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
